violations.description: Dangerous checkout of untrusted PR code in pull_request_target workflow
violations.evidence: pull_request_target trigger allows access to secrets; checking out PR head ref and repo allows executing untrusted code with secret access.
violations.recommendation: Use the pull_request trigger instead, or if pull_request_target is necessary, use the base ref (default checkout) and only check files/data, not execute them.

violations.description: Excessive workflow-level permissions (write-all) in pull_request_target workflow
violations.evidence: permissions: write-all is used in a pull_request_target workflow, granting unnecessary excessive write access to the GITHUB_TOKEN.
violations.recommendation: Use the minimal required permissions (e.g., permissions: { pull-requests: write }).

violations.description: Untrusted GitHub event data interpolated into shell script
violations.evidence: Untrusted input from issues event (github.event.issue.title and github.event.issue.body) is directly interpolated into a bash run script.
violations.recommendation: Use environment variables to pass untrusted input to shell scripts (e.g., env: { ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ ... }} } and then use "$ISSUE_TITLE" in the script).

violations.description: Usage of self-hosted runner for build and deployment tasks
violations.evidence: Workflow runs on self-hosted runners which persist state between jobs, posing significant risk of credential theft and persistence for build/deploy workflows.
violations.recommendation: Use GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners for CI/CD tasks to ensure environment isolation.
